$schema_note: Physical-roof audit of every pre-existing (non-recon_*) 1835 structure record. inventory_roof_count is the number deducted from the 665-roof programme; attached ranges remain one inventory roof unless the source describes distinct buildings.

method.eligible: A covered building or independently roofed working structure plausibly standing on the scene date.
method.ineligible: Open ground/enclosure, bridge, pier, incomplete roofless works, or a building whose July existence is contradicted by the production chronology.
method.compound: roof_count records distinct physical roof masses; inventory_roof_count counts attached ranges as one roofed building but counts separately described cabins separately.
method.substitution: Each eligible existing inventory roof explicitly replaces that many anonymous programme slots in its district/family; it is not added above 665.

T-0883. One gable roof on the garrison's barn, placed off the 1830 Harrison plan and corroborated in position by Hubbard. A2 (barn or carriage shed) IS READ OFF THE FUNCTION AND NOT THE BAND: 47 x 31 ft stands above A2's 18-26 by 28-44 ft on both axes, which is what a plate that calls a building BIG should produce, and no wider family fits a barn. THE FORT COLUMN IS FULL AND THIS ROOF IS NOT IN IT. The inventory's district matrix authorises ten roofs in the fort district, all of them under fort_principal, and ten stand — this building is the eleventh, twelfth or thirteenth. It substitutes no anonymous slot and the zero is deliberate: the fort column's own text says 'ten principal roofs in the custom Fort Dearborn compound', and these three are service buildings on the reservation OUTSIDE the pickets, which that sentence never counted. They are additions above the district's estimate, which is what the programme file's exceedance report exists to report.

T-1036. One gable roof on the United States factory, 152 m south of the pickets, where the 1830 Harrison plan letters `U.S. Factor's House` against three blocks and this record builds the one the label touches. C2 (store-residence) IS CHOSEN BECAUSE IT NAMES WHAT A FACTORY WAS AND NOTHING MORE — the government's trading house, a shop and a dwelling in one building — and because it is the only family in the crosswalk that puts trade and living under one roof without naming a trade. THE BAND DOES NOT FIT AND THE FAMILY IS TAKEN ANYWAY: 67 x 26 ft is far outside C2's 18x30-22x40 ft and its 1.5 levels against this building's two, exactly as W4's band does not fit the shop and A5's does not fit out building (a). F2 (narrow two-storey warehouse, 20x40-26x60 ft, two levels) fits the numbers much better and was refused on the label: a warehouse is a use, this building is attested as a factor's HOUSE with a family living in it from 1822, and a family label here is a roof-counting convenience while a use would be a claim. Confidence is low: the roof itself is invented (L231), and the building's own witnesses say nothing about it. THE FORT COLUMN IS FULL AND THIS ROOF IS NOT IN IT. The inventory's district matrix authorises ten roofs in the fort district, all under fort_principal, and ten stand — this is one more above them, on the same footing as the three service buildings T-0883 added and the two out buildings T-0881 added. It substitutes no anonymous slot and the zero is deliberate: the fort column's own text says 'ten principal roofs in the custom Fort Dearborn compound', and this building stands on the reservation OUTSIDE the pickets, which that sentence never counted. It is an addition above the district's estimate, which is what the programme file's exceedance report exists to report.

Documented two-story frame inn on Lake Street near Wells, one principal roof — the same reading as tremont_house_1 and exchange_coffee_house. Andreas p. 635 has it built in 1834 and opened by Johnson and Stevens, and the Chicago American of 13 June 1835 advertises two professional offices in it seventeen days before the scene date, so it is a covered building standing on 1 July 1835 and eligible. It is a PRE-EXISTING roof, not a reconstructed one: the town this project models already had it, so it substitutes an anonymous T2 slot rather than adding to the target. T2 is the frontier-inn family — two storeys, clapboard frame, 5-8 bays — which is what Andreas's 'two-story building, with eaves to the street' describes; T1 is the lower one-and-a-half-storey public house and T3 is the Sauganash's single custom asset, and neither fits. No stable is attested here, so no A1 roof is claimed with it (T2's own crosswalk note forbids adding one silently).

T-0133. A reconstructed freight shed on the north bank at the Dearborn crossing, built from image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18 ('low warehouses on the banks'). It is an eligible physical roof and it is counted as one, in the north district under family F1 (freight or storage shed). IT SUBSTITUTES NO ANONYMOUS SLOT AND THE FIGURE IS ZERO ON PURPOSE: the inventory's district matrix allows the north division ONE warehouse-or-freight roof and the Kinzie and Hunter forwarding store already stands on it, so there is no north freight slot for this roof to replace. It is therefore an addition above the district's estimate rather than a substitution inside it, which is what the plate asks for and what the programme file's own exceedance report is for.

T-1636. A reconstructed freight shed on the SOUTH bank at the Dearborn reach, the south-bank half of the four north-bank sheds above and built from the same plate — image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18, 'low warehouses on the banks', which draws them on BOTH banks. It stands on the 9.5 m of town ground between South Water Street's platted end and State Street's corridor, ground that was a channel of this reconstruction's own making until T-1629 filled it back to the bank Wright drew. It is an eligible physical roof and it is counted as one, in the south district under family F1 (freight or storage shed). IT SUBSTITUTES ONE ANONYMOUS SLOT, and the figure is one rather than the north sheds' zero for the reason T-0283 recorded when it moved six freight roofs from this very cell: the South's warehouses_freight row still carries unbuilt, unnamed slots, and an authored slot yields to a record that names a building. So this roof is a re-typing inside the programme's size rather than an addition above it, and the town's roof total does not move for it.

T-1640. The SECOND reconstructed freight shed on the south bank at the Dearborn reach, standing on the same two walls as south_bank_shed_dearborn_e1 above and 5.20 m behind it, with a loading yard between the two. It is built from the same plate and from the one thing that plate holds in the plural — image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18 draws low warehouseS on both banks, and the north bank has four of them. It stands on the terrace BEHIND the bank strip rather than on the strip itself, because tools/measure_south_bank_ground.py reports that the strip's own one remaining position stands on the ground e1's wagon door opens onto; docs/LIBERTIES.md L281 owns that reasoning. It is an eligible physical roof and it is counted as one, in the south district under family F1 (freight or storage shed). IT SUBSTITUTES ONE ANONYMOUS SLOT, for e1's reason exactly: the South's warehouses_freight row still carries unbuilt, unnamed slots — four of them before this roof — and an authored slot yields to a record that names a building. So this roof is a re-typing inside the programme's size rather than an addition above it, and the town's roof total does not move for it.

T-1709. The packing and barrelling house of the South Branch works, standing 5.20 m south of `newberry_dole_slaughterhouse_south_branch` across a cart yard. One roof, and it is counted in the SOUTH district under family W3 - the crosswalk's cooper, wagon and wheelwright shop, whose visible signature is hoops and barrels, which is what a packing house is full of between seasons. IT SUBSTITUTES ONE ANONYMOUS SLOT, on the same reasoning every named works building here takes: the South's workshops row still carries unbuilt, unnamed W3 slots and an authored slot yields to a record that names a building. So this roof is a re-typing inside the programme's size and the town's roof total does not move for it.
